clue.text: Crustacean expert reflected on day with school

indicators.note: in an across clue, sitting on something means coming straight after it

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for day

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word for expert is read from its end

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A marine biologist looks back on a day spent with a class of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests pupils, but here it is the collective noun for whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A decapod is a ten-legged creature such as a crab, lobster or shrimp.

clue.text: Brother in car after party half-drunk

indicators.note: only half of the word for drunk is kept, the back three letters dropped
the car word follows the party word in the answer

parts.note: a do is an informal party
the Mini is a classic small British car
canned is slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: A monk rides in a car after a party, somewhat tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: DO + MINI + CAN, the first half of CANNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a friar of the order founded by Saint Dominic, addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Clubs performing well toe the line

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
on form means playing at one's best

explanation.surface: A golfer whose clubs are behaving keeps toeing the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe the line is an idiom for obeying the rules, which is to comply with expected standards.

clue.text: Gem lettuce originally topped with fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, being topped means having another piece placed above it

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word lettuce, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of lettuce

explanation.surface: A Little Gem lettuce served with fruit on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Gem looks like part of 'Little Gem', a lettuce variety, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious lustrous jewel formed inside an oyster.

clue.text: Medic held up sister regularly in shift?

parts.note: DR is short for doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding something up turns it to read from bottom to top
regularly means taking every other letter of the word sister

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of sister

explanation.surface: A doctor kept a nurse waiting during a hospital shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medic' and 'sister' suggest a hospital ward, and 'shift' a working period; it is in fact a loose dress, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple straight-cut frock, one example of a garment women wear.

clue.text: Son follows old lady cycling to get flask

indicators.note: the son abbreviation comes after the other piece
cycling moves the front letters of the word round to the back

parts.note: old lady is informal for one's mother
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother goes cycling and her son tags along to fetch a drinks flask.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTHER with its first two letters moved to the end gives THERMO, then S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum-insulated bottle that keeps drinks hot or cold; the brand name became generic.

clue.text: Practitioner's charge collected by the first

indicators.note: something collected by another is gathered up inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'
1ST, with the numeral read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A professional's fee is the first thing to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first' is written THE 1ST, and the charge sits between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist is someone who treats patients professionally, a practitioner of a healing discipline.

clue.text: Beetle finally moving under can for survival

indicators.note: letters that are moving do not stay in their printed order
in a down clue, under means coming after
finally points to the last letter of the word beetle

parts.note: last letter of beetle
the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A beetle crawls under a tin can to stay alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' does double duty here: it is part of the anagram fodder as well as positioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the ability to last and keep going, which is what survival requires.

clue.text: Police force adopting popular sergeant's attitudes

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular noun that can mean a set of attitudes

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the police word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
in means fashionable
DS stands for detective sergeant

explanation.surface: The police take on the views of a well-liked sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met, short for London's Metropolitan Police, is the force that takes in the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's established way of thinking, their collected outlook and beliefs.

clue.text: Look of gloom from second hood

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: A second hooded figure casts a gloomy glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowl is an angry frown, a facial expression of displeasure.

clue.text: Person near Senegal mostly recycled metal

indicators.note: near means placed right beside, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a man is a person

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade in a new form
mostly means all but the last letter of the country's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone living near Senegal mostly recycles metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a hard grey chemical element, number 25, classed among the transition metals.

clue.text: Couple patrolling centre of Pinner search me

indicators.note: patrolling means going all around an area, so it surrounds

parts.note: a duo is a pair

indicators.note: centre of keeps only the middle pair of the six letters

parts.note: middle two letters of Pinner

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers on patrol in central Pinner are clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinner is a suburb of north-west London; only its middle pair of letters is used.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Search me' and the colloquial contraction of 'don't know' are both casual ways of admitting ignorance.

clue.text: Pole loads food you might get from a bar

definitions.text: food you might get from a bar

parts.note: N is the North Pole
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: A Polish man piles up food at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is not a pub but a noodle bar, an eatery serving Asian dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle bars are casual restaurants serving bowls of pasta-like strips in broth.

clue.text: Adult touchy about contents of gold spray can?

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: about suggests turning around, so the word for touchy is read backwards

parts.note: sore can mean irritable or sensitive

indicators.note: contents means only the inner letters of gold, its outer pair dropped

parts.note: the middle letters of gold

explanation.surface: A grown-up is sensitive about what's inside a gold spray-paint can.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised container releasing a fine mist; the question mark flags the punning question 'can spray?'.

clue.text: Flattening of school on South Island boy catches

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside, so the boy surrounds the island letter

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a UK state secondary school
re means concerning, about
S for south
a son is a boy
I for island

explanation.surface: A school on a southern island is flattened, and a boy is caught up.
explanation.walkthrough: A comp is a British comprehensive school; 'on' here means concerning, the usual RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Compression is the squeezing of something into a smaller, flatter shape.

clue.text: Correct rug inscribed with name in blue

parts.note: right means correct

indicators.note: inscribed with means having something written into it, so the name goes inside

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee
N for name

explanation.surface: A proper rug embroidered with a name in blue thread.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain blue is the colour of the Conservative Party, so blue means conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in UK politics signals Tory, and right-wing means holding conservative political views.

clue.text: Nick reportedly over in base upset abrasive cleaner

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word for nick is taken by its sound

parts.note: to nick is to steal, which sounds like a metal

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read upwards
the over abbreviation is put inside the word for base

parts.note: base means low, mean
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Steal some upset scouring pads from a nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for steal (and for prison).
explanation.definitionFit: Steel wool is a pad of fine metal strands used to scour and polish surfaces.

clue.text: Fine wiping out husband's money

indicators.note: wiping out a thing removes it entirely from the word

parts.note: fine means thin, slender
H for husband

explanation.surface: A penalty that wipes out a husband's savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests a penalty, but it means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is old British slang for cash.

clue.text: Fresh herb selection bought at last shop

parts.note: fresh means new
sage is a herb

indicators.note: at last keeps only the final letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: last letters of selection and bought

explanation.surface: A selection of fresh herbs finally bought at a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a newsagent is a corner shop selling papers, sweets and tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a retail outlet selling newspapers and magazines, a kind of store.

clue.text: Bill and his TV partner returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of children's TV

explanation.surface: Bill and Ben, the Flowerpot Men, come back on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben was a British children's TV show about two flowerpot puppets.
explanation.definitionFit: Neb is a dialect word for a bird's beak, which is also called its bill.

clue.text: Steal profit put beneath counter

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece beneath another places it later

parts.note: a bar is a serving counter
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Profits hidden under a shop counter are as good as stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is something bought very cheaply, a real deal at a low price.

clue.text: Relative became stuck with a silly pet hen

indicators.note: something silly is muddled, so these letters get jumbled
the word for became is stuck around the other letters, holding them in place

parts.note: grew means became, as in grew tired
taken as written
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A relation got stuck with a daft pet chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-nephew is the grandson of one's sibling, a family member.

clue.text: One who's taken stockings with label inside

indicators.note: the label goes inside the stockings word

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A shoplifter takes stockings with the price label still inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken' hints at shoplifting; here it means captured.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person seized and held captive as security for a demand.

clue.text: Soup child's left outside of awful ex-reform facility

indicators.note: child's left means the child has gone away, removing it

parts.note: borscht is beetroot soup
CH is the abbreviation for child

indicators.note: outside of keeps only the outer letters of awful

parts.note: first and last letters of awful

explanation.surface: A child has left behind some awful soup at a former reform school.
explanation.walkthrough: BORSCHT without CH, then AL. A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders, abolished in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: Borstals were British institutions for reforming youthful offenders, now closed, hence ex-.

clue.text: Fuse outside left one with a fair shock?

indicators.note: the fuse word sits outside, around the letter for left

parts.note: to bond is to join together, fuse
L for left

explanation.surface: Wiring a fuse badly leaves someone with a nasty shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock here is a mass of hair, not an electrical jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A blond is a person with pale yellow hair; a shock of hair is a thick mop.

clue.text: It's played across Toscana stadium

indicators.note: across means spanning the gap between the words, where the letters run on

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A match is played in a Tuscan stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Toscana is the Italian name for Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type card game, something people play.

clue.text: Primate's Greek cross maybe raised after noon

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means turned upward, read from the bottom

parts.note: PM means post meridiem, after midday

explanation.surface: An archbishop's Greek cross is lifted in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop with a cross, but it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimp, short for chimpanzee, is an African ape and so a primate.

clue.text: Green area of church the setter occupies

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit inside it

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The setter sits in a grassy part of the churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or gullible, which is what naive describes.

clue.text: Arab very shortly heading to port

indicators.note: port is the left side, so heading that way in an across clue reads right to left

parts.note: in a mo means in a moment

explanation.surface: An Arab ship will very soon set course for harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman, an Arab state on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Start agitating toerag in Italy

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; a toerag is British slang for a scoundrel
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone starts stirring up a lowlife in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a positional word, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or arise, so it is a verb meaning to commence.

clue.text: Fellow covering for leader in Royal County

indicators.note: covering for means standing in, so the fellow word replaces the first letter

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
regal means royal

explanation.surface: A fellow stands in for the head of the Royal County.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal County' reads as a set phrase (Meath's nickname), but Royal belongs to the wordplay. Donegal is in north-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is an Irish administrative region in Ulster, one of the island's thirty-two counties.

clue.text: Official tense when king advances

indicators.note: advances means the king letter moves forward to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: the perfect is a grammatical tense
R for rex, king

explanation.surface: An official gets tense whenever the king approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: PERFECT with its R moved one place forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefect is an administrative officer, as in a French prefect, or a senior school monitor.
